title: Kripke completeness for equality-free intuitionistic first-order logic
summary: Build a varying-domain term countermodel for every failed equality-free native deduction, retaining arbitrary premises and the original free names.
abstract: A world may accept a first-order assertion only after acquiring more objects or more information. Kripke completeness says that this changing-information semantics captures exactly intuitionistic deduction: whenever an equality-free conclusion has no proof from its premises, one world can force every premise while failing that conclusion. We construct such worlds from prime theories and give them actual terms as objects. The truth argument handles present existential witnesses and future universal counterinstances, then returns to any countable original supply of names. For a countable language this yields strong completeness for arbitrary premise sets, rooted countermodels and finite-premise semantic consequences.
